subjects.name: Software Engineering
subjects.courseObjective: To understand the phases of software development and project management.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Understand the software lifecycle models
CO2: Elicit and document requirements in SRS
CO3: Design software using structured tools
CO4: Test software systems using black-box and white-box methods
CO5: Manage projects using estimation models like COCOMO
textbooks: Roger S. Pressman, 'Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach', McGraw-Hill
Rajib Mall, 'Fundamentals of Software Engineering', PHI

subjects.name: Design & Analysis of Algorithms
subjects.courseObjective: To design efficient algorithms and analyze their time/space complexity.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Apply asymptotic notations to analyze algorithm efficiency
CO2: Implement and compare search/sort methods
CO3: Design algorithms using greedy, divide & conquer, and dynamic programming
CO4: Solve graph problems like shortest path and minimum spanning trees
CO5: Explain P, NP, NP-complete classes and Cook's theorem
textbooks: T.H. Cormen, C.E. Leiserson, R.L. Rivest, and C. Stein, 'Introduction to Algorithms', MIT Press
Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni and Sanguthevar Rajasekaran, 'Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms', Universities Press
references: Anany Levitin, 'Introduction to the Design and Analysis of Algorithms', Pearson Education

subjects.name: Full-stack Development II
subjects.courseObjective: To master modern single-page applications using React.js and Angular.js frameworks.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Build UIs using React functional/class components
CO2: Style React applications and configure client-side routing
CO3: Manage form state and handle dynamic browser events
CO4: Fetch and bind external API data in React and Angular
CO5: Write custom directives, controllers, and services in AngularJS
textbooks: Kirupa Chinnathambi, 'Learning React: A Hands-On Guide to Building Web Applications Using React and Redux', Addison-Wesley
Brad Green and Shyam Seshadri, 'AngularJS', O'Reilly Media
references: React and Angular Official Documentation websites

subjects.name: Machine Learning
subjects.courseObjective: To understand machine learning principles, algorithms, and practical applications.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Formulate business problems as machine learning tasks
CO2: Apply supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning concepts
CO3: Design ML pipelines including data preparation and training
CO4: Deploy ML pilot projects for real-world enterprise scenarios
CO5: Construct ensemble methods like Bagging, Boosting, and Random Forest
textbooks: Ethem Alpaydin, 'Introduction to Machine Learning', MIT Press
references: Stephen Marsland, 'Machine Learning: An Algorithmic Perspective', CRC Press
